case_name: Nallagondla Kanthamma vs Nallagondala Rajyam And Ors.
facts_of_case: The plaintiff claimed to be the legally wedded wife of Nallagondla Penchalaiah who died while working in Integral Coach Factory, Madras. She sought declaration that she is entitled to receive benefits due to her husband's death and also for permanent injunction and mandatory injunction.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to receive notices does not necessarily mean they are unaware of the proceedings.
legal_principles.held: Though he did not express his willingness, the plaintiff went to him at Madras hoping that her destiny is with him only as a dutiful Indian wife. She soon found that her husband is having illicit intimacy with one married woman viz., Rajyam who was already big with four children through her husband.

legal_principles.principle: A party's admission to a fact does not necessarily mean they are aware of all related facts.
legal_principles.held: An admission was made that as per the records in Crl.M.P. No. 72/88, these defendants paid Rs. 367/- per month to the plaintiff towards her maintenance, but however, they are not aware of the proceedings M.C. No. 3/95.

outcome.final_order: The plaintiff and the third defendant are equally entitled to receive the benefits due to the deceased Penchalaiah from the office of Integral Coach Factory, Perambur, Madras. The widows are entitled to receive in equal shares.
